sanskrit: apāsmād brāhmaṇīsandhām apadhārān ni dadhmasi | indrāgnī naḥ savedasāv arṇavād adhi muñcatām ||
english: Away from us we thrust the Brāhmaṇīsandhā, we drive off the obstructing torrents; may Indra and Agni, united in treasure, release us from the flood.

sanskrit: namas te brāhmaṇīsandhe parehi yata eyatha yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmas taṃ te pra suvāmi tam adhi pra sūtāḥ ||
english: Homage to you, O Brāhmaṇīsandhā — go back whence you have come. He who hates us and him whom we hate, upon him I urge you forward; be you roused against him.

sanskrit: apāraṃ tvāhur arṇavam anināyāṃ na ye viduḥ | yas te vedodaram āsyaṃ mahat sākṣād veda mukhaṃ tava niyājaṃ tava te viduḥ ||
english: They call you a boundless ocean — those who do not lead rightly do not know you; but those who directly know your belly, your great mouth, your face, your rite of dismissal — they truly know you.

sanskrit: indreṇa kl̥ptā yonir narako asyāḥ kulāyam | mahān samudro rajaso vimānaḥ svarge loke api naḥ kṛṇotu ||
english: Her womb has been fashioned by Indra; hell is her nest. May the great ocean, the measurer of the atmospheric realm, grant us a place in the celestial world as well.

sanskrit: tasyaudanasya bṛhaspatiḥ śiro brahma mukhaṃ sūryācandramasāv akṣyau bṛhadrathantare śrotre | agnir āsyaṃ vidyuj jihvā maruto dantāḥ pavamānaḥ prāṇaḥ ||
english: Of that odana: Bṛhaspati is the head, Brahman the face, the Sun and Moon the two eyes, the Bṛhat and Rathantara sāmans the two ears; Agni is the mouth, lightning the tongue, the Maruts the teeth, Pavamāna the breath.

sanskrit: oṣadhayo lomāni vanaspatayaḥ keśāḥ samudro mūtram aśvinā prapade | caruṃ pañcabilam ukhaṃ gharmam abhīndhe ||
english: The herbs are the body-hairs, the trees the head-hair, the ocean the urine, the two Aśvins the fore-feet; the caruvessel is the five-holed cooking-pot, the gharma is kindled here.

sanskrit: cakṣur musalaṃ kāma ulūkhalaṃ ditiḥ śūrpam aditiḥ śūrpagrāhī vāto apāvinak | gāvas taṇḍulā aśvāḥ kaṇā maśakās tuṣāḥ kabru phalīkaraṇāḥ śyāmam ayo lohitam ayo 'sya māṃsam ||
english: The eye is the pestle, Desire the mortar, Diti the winnowing-fan, Aditi the one who grasps the winnowing-fan, the Wind has winnowed it clean; the cows are the husked grains, the horses the broken fragments, the gnats the chaff, the kabru and phalīkaraṇa plants the dark iron, the red iron his flesh.

sanskrit: trapu bhasmārjunam asthīni haritaṃ varṇaḥ puṣkalaṃ gandhaḥ | khalaḥ pātram uṣṭārau bāhū sphyāv aṃsau gudā varatrā īṣānūkyaṃ yugāni jatravaḥ ||
english: Tin is the ash, the white substances are the bones, green is the complexion, abundant is the fragrance; the threshing-floor is the vessel, the two camels the arms, the two wooden spoons the shoulders, the traces the intestines, the pole and the yoke-pin the cross-pieces, the yoke-beams the collar-bones.

sanskrit: ṛtaṃ hastābhiṣecanaṃ kulyopasecanam ārtavāḥ paktāro agniḥ prāśītā brāhmaṇaḥ pratigrahītā ||
english: Sacred truth is the hand-sprinkling, the channel-water is the pouring over; the seasonal rains are the cookers, Fire is the eater, the Brāhmaṇa is the receiver.

sanskrit: tasyaudanasya bhūmiḥ kumbhī dyaur apidhānaṃ śiro 'bhram ūṣmā nīhāro bṛhad āyavanaṃ rathantaraṃ darviḥ | diśaḥ pārśve sītāḥ parśavaḥ sikatā ūbadhyaṃ palalam upastaraṇam ahorātre vikramaṇe odanasya ||
english: Of that odana: the Earth is the cooking-pot, Heaven the lid, the head the cloud, steam the mist; the Bṛhat is the spreading base, the Rathantara the ladle; the quarters are the flanks, the furrows the ribs, the sand the lower fat, the sesamum paste the under-layer, day and night the two strides of the odana.

sanskrit: varṣaṃ prokṣaṇaṃ marutaḥ paryaindhata kiṣkaravaḥ paridhayaḥ | ṛcā kumbhy adhidhīyata ārtvijyena preṣyate brahmaṇā prati gṛhyate ||
english: Rain is the sprinkling-water, the Maruts have kindled it round about, the kiṣkara-grasses are the enclosing sticks; by the ṛc-verse the pot is placed upon the fire, by the priestly office it is dispatched, by Brahman it is received.

sanskrit: ya etasyaudanasyaivaṃ mahimānaṃ vidyāt | nālpa iti brūyān nānupasecana iti nedaṃ ca kiṃ ceti ||
english: Whoever should thus know the greatness of this odana — he should not say it is small, nor say it is mere sprinkling-over, nor say this is nothing whatsoever.

sanskrit: yāvad dātābhimanasyet taṃ nātivadet | odanena yajñavacaḥ sarve lokāḥ samāpyāḥ ||
english: As much as the giver might intend in his mind, that he should not overspeak; by the odana, the sacrificial word, all worlds are fulfilled.

sanskrit: yasmin samudro dyaur bhūmis trayo 'varaparaṃ śritāḥ ||
english: In whom the ocean, heaven, and earth — the three — rest, lower and upper alike.
